How to use GIS One Map Animator

Step-by-step guides for the whole workflow, then every element in the Layers → Add panel — what it does, an example frame, its settings panel, how to place it, its animations and the settings you can change. Click a picture to see it full size.

Getting started

🚀 Start a project

  1. On the home page type a name and press Create, or press ✨ Auto video and describe the video in one sentence.
  2. You land in the editor. The six steps at the top are the workflow: Route · Layers · Look · Signs · Camera · Preview & export.
  3. Everything saves automatically in your browser. Use Save file (top right) to keep a .json copy, and Open file on the home page to open it again.

✏ Draw a route (optional)

  1. In 1 Route, click on the map to place points — the line curves through them by itself.
  2. Or press Use a route file for GPX, KML/KMZ, IGC or GeoJSON.
  3. Drag a point to move it, double-click a point for a sharp corner, click a point to pause there or split the leg.
  4. Legs (top right) set how you travel — walk, car, ferry, plane… each with its own symbol.
  5. No route needed? Press Skip and go straight to layers.

🧩 Add layers (elements)

  1. In 2 Layers → Add, open a section and click an element (all of them are explained below).
  2. Follow the hint at the top of the map: click a place, click along a line, or click around an area and press Finish.
  3. The new layer opens its settings on the left. Every layer has Timing & animation and When it shows: *Shows from*, *Animates for*, *Hides at*, *Stays until the end*, and Split at the playhead to show it only for part of the scene.
  4. Boxes, labels, legends and cards can be dragged on the video. Use Layers to show/hide, lock, reorder or delete.

🎨 Choose the look

  1. In 3 Look pick a Map theme (Classic, Dark, Satellite, Night…) and extras: place names, 3D mountains, globe, sky & clouds, 3D buildings.
  2. Set the route line colour, width and the travelling symbol.
  3. Each scene has its own look; a new scene copies the last one.

🪧 Add signs

  1. In 4 Signs press + Add sign, pick a style, click where it goes and type the text.
  2. Choose when it appears: when the line gets there, from the start, at the end or at a set time.

🎥 Set up the camera

  1. In 5 Camera choose a movement: Fixed view, Start to end, Keyframes, Rotate globe, Orbit or Follow the line.
  2. For keyframes: move the playhead, frame the view (drag, zoom, right-drag to rotate, tilt) and press ◆ Add keyframe at the playhead. Drag the diamonds on the timeline to retime them.
  3. Add start & end moves (zoom in from space / the country…) and lens effects (depth of field, vignette).

🎬 Scenes, transitions and the full preview

  1. Press + New scene in the top bar for another part of the story; each scene has its own route, layers, look and camera.
  2. In 6 Preview & export set To the next scene (dissolve, slide, zoom, wipe, circle, blur, flash…) and its length.
  3. Press All scenes in the timeline bar (or Shift+Space) to watch every scene together with the logo strip, ticker and sound running across them.

🏷 Logo strip, ticker and sound

  1. In 6 Preview & export → Logo & lower third: turn the logo strip on, replace it with your own wide PNG, and fill the lower third (country, place, date, ticker text separated by |).
  2. They run continuously across all scenes — the slide-in only happens at the very start.
  3. Sound is off by default: turn it on for automatic effects (explosions, engines, HUD beeps, typing) and a background score; add music or record a voiceover.

📤 Preview and export the video

  1. Pick a Preset (YouTube 1080p/4K, Reels 9:16, Instagram 4:5, Square, Cinema 21:9…) or set resolution and frame rate.
  2. Press Render — the MP4 is made in your browser; nothing is uploaded. Keep the tab open while it renders.
  3. Save this frame as PNG gives a still for a thumbnail.

✨ Auto video from one sentence

  1. Press ✨ Auto video and describe it: places, date and what happened (e.g. “Train collision at Urda on the Madrid–Seville line, 28 October 2026”).
  2. Press Find the places, check the plan, pick the building blocks (route A→B, ripples, before/after images, weather, ticker, basemap, music).
  3. Press Create the video — you get editable scenes you can change like any other project.

📰 News desk · AI — a news video from today’s incidents

  1. Press 📰 News desk on the home page or in the top bar. It lists today’s floods, fires, earthquakes, landslides, disasters and migration incidents — or type a topic and press Search now.
  2. Pick a story and check the place, date and building blocks: fly to the place, before / after satellite, damage & analysis, photos and videos.
  3. Optional: ✨ Write with AI writes the voice-over, title, description and hashtags (add your own Anthropic key in AI settings; a free NASA FIRMS key adds live fire hotspots).
  4. Press Create the video — or 🔥 Auto fire video / 🌊 Auto flood video for one click. You get normal scenes you can edit.

🧭 GEO·BRIEF news layout (intro, zoom, pre & post, photos)

  1. News videos are built from briefing frames: Intro over a globe, Zoom to location, a full view with title block and mini globe, Pre & post (before / after with dates), a photo slideshow with captions and credits, and an end card. Add any of them from Layers → Add → Typography.
  2. Every part of a frame is its own layer — drag the title block, globe, panels or photos on the video and change their text, pictures, dates and credits in the settings.
  3. The breaking-news ticker is off by default; switch it on in the frame settings when you want it.
  4. Zoom-to-location scenes use a steady 2D map. In Camera → zoom settings set Map while zooming to Globe if you prefer the globe.

🛰 Site watch — ports and air bases from orbit

  1. Press 🛰 Site watch. Pick a ready-made site from ⚡ Ready now (refreshed twice a month) or any port, naval base or air base from the list or the map.
  2. Choose the imagery — Esri, Sentinel-2 or Sentinel-1 radar — and what to count: ships or aircraft. The clearest pass of every month is picked; hazy or odd passes are set aside, and you can correct any count.
  3. Create the story: zoom to the site, a pass grid with an overview map (it zooms into one pass), a flip-through, a pre & post swipe, a dashboard with the counts and an end card.

🗂 Map layer stack — exploded GIS layers

  1. In Layers → Add → Cartography → Map layer stack, click Layer stack from your pictures and choose your layer pictures at once (or try the Seattle sample).
  2. The flat map tilts, the layers float apart, then each one is shown in turn with its name and source; at the end every layer is labelled.
  3. In the settings set each layer’s name, source, colour, opacity and order, and the Shape (square, rounded, circle, oval, hexagon, octagon, diamond), rotate, tilt, zoom, gap, slow turn, title and a sources list. Drag the stack on the video to move it.

🔍 Magnifier lens on a photo or the map

  1. Add Lens / zoom inset and set What the lens shows to Magnifier.
  2. Set The spot it looks at to A spot on the screen and drag the small ring onto the photo or before / after picture — or keep it on a place on the map.
  3. Choose the Magnification (1.2–12×) and the shape (round lens, rectangle, card, glass bubble); drag the lens where you want it.

All elements 619

Example frames were made with the default settings on a plain test map — on your map they sit on the basemap you choose. Elements that need your own files or a live data service show their settings instead.

✏️ Draw or place 10

⬡Boundary

Boundary · boundary

Outline of a country, city or any region

Step by step

  1. Click the button.
  2. Click around the area on the map — each click adds a corner.
  3. Press Finish to close the shape.
  4. Open When it shows to set when it appears, how long it animates and when it hides (or Split at the playhead).

🌃Night roads map

Glowing roads at night · nightroads

The road network lights up like a city at night.

Step by step

  1. Frame the city.
  2. Click the button — the roads in view glow.
  3. Set colour and glow in the settings.
  4. Open When it shows to set when it appears, how long it animates and when it hides (or Split at the playhead).
Needs your own data or a live service — see the steps

🟦Population mosaic

Smart map · smartmap

A data map of a region: mosaic cells, hot spots, potential sites, drive times, revenue halos, heat map or sized circles.

Step by step

  1. Click the button for the kind of smart map you want.
  2. Click around the region on the map, then press Finish.
  3. It fills with sample data first — load your own CSV or GeoJSON in the layer settings.
  4. A second smart map re-uses the same region and data automatically.
  5. Open When it shows to set when it appears, how long it animates and when it hides (or Split at the playhead).

🏙Digital twin city (white)

Digital twin city · twin

The city’s real buildings (OpenStreetMap) in a stylised 3D look — clay, hologram, blueprint, night gold, magenta, height colours or traffic trails.

Step by step

  1. Click the button — the map switches to Dark for the look (change it in Look).
  2. Click the centre of the city.
  3. Buildings load from OpenStreetMap (needs internet); set the radius, look, title and pulses in the settings.
  4. Open When it shows to set when it appears, how long it animates and when it hides (or Split at the playhead).

🛰 Imagery & remote sensing 18

Images: PNG/JPG (with a .pgw/.jgw/.wld world file), GeoTIFF (e.g. a Sentinel scene downloaded from Copernicus Browser), or KML/KMZ ground overlays — or any picture you line up by hand. Videos on the map: MP4 / WebM, line up the four corners.

🖼Georeferenced image

Georeferenced image · image

A picture, scan, drone photo or GeoTIFF fitted onto the map.

Step by step

  1. Click the button and choose the file (PNG/JPG with a world file, GeoTIFF, KML/KMZ ground overlay — or any picture).
  2. Georeferenced files land in the right place; otherwise drag its four corners onto matching places on the map.
  3. Set opacity, blend and the reveal (fade / wipe).
  4. Open When it shows to set when it appears, how long it animates and when it hides (or Split at the playhead).

💡 PNG/JPG with a .pgw/.jgw world file, GeoTIFF and KML/KMZ ground overlays are placed automatically.

Fade inWipe inNo animation

Settings you can change

ImageOpacityBlendWipe fromBorderBorder colour

◐Before / after

Before / after · compare

Swipe or fade between a pre and a post image — e.g. satellite pictures before and after a disaster.

Step by step

  1. Click the button and choose the BEFORE picture, then the AFTER picture.
  2. Line them up by dragging the corners (or use georeferenced files).
  3. Pick swipe or fade, the direction and how many times it goes back and forth; turn on full screen if you like.
  4. Drag the BEFORE / AFTER tags on the video.
  5. Open When it shows to set when it appears, how long it animates and when it hides (or Split at the playhead).

💡 Use two pictures of the same place (before / after). Drag the BEFORE / AFTER tags on the video.

🛰Satellite through time

Satellite through time · wayback

Esri World Imagery Wayback: real satellite pictures of the same place from different years, cross-fading with a date label.

Real scenes (Planetary Computer) · pc

Microsoft Planetary Computer: lists every real Sentinel / Landsat acquisition over your view with date, cloud cover and a thumbnail.

🛰Live satellite (GOES / Meteosat)

Live weather-satellite pictures (GOES, Meteosat, Himawari) of the last hours as a loop.

  4. Open When it shows to set when it appears, how long it animates and when it hides (or Split at the playhead).

✈Weapon reveal — drone, rename SHAHED → GERAN

Weapon reveal · mgweapon

A drone, missile, jet, tank or ship drawn as a crimson blueprint: wireframe, fill, a letter-spaced name that decodes (and can be renamed, e.g. SHAHED → GERAN), callouts with leader lines, a magnifier circle on a part and a spec table

Step by step

  1. Click the button — the weapon appears as a crimson blueprint.

  4. Open When it shows to set when it appears, how long it animates and when it hides (or Split at the playhead).

🗂Layer stack from your pictures (choose several)

Map layer stack · layerstack

Your map layers (imagery, streets, water, trees, buildings, boundaries …) as one flat map that tilts, floats apart into a 3D stack and shows each layer in turn with its name and source

Step by step

  1. Click the button and choose your layer pictures — several at once (transparent PNGs of the same area work best).
  2. Name files like 0_Imagery.png, 1_Streets.png: the number sets the order (bottom → top), the rest becomes the label.
  3. In the settings: names, sources, colour, opacity and order of each layer; Shape (square, circle, oval, hexagon…), rotate, tilt, zoom, gap, slow turn, title and a sources list.
  4. Drag the stack on the video to move it. Press Fit the time to the layers for about 2 s per layer.
  5. Open When it shows to set when it appears, how long it animates and when it hides (or Split at the playhead).

💡 The Seattle sample buttons load six ready layers and an overview picture, with their sources.

Animations

Overview → flat map → tilt → float apart → each layer in turnFlat map → tilt → float apart (no tour)Already apart — each layer in turnLayers drop in one by oneFade in (stack shown)Shown

Settings you can change

Overview picture to start fromOverview captionShape of each layerTurn the shape (°)Thin edge on every layerRotateTiltZoomSpace between layersSlow turn while it playsPosition ←→Position ↑↓Zoom on the layer being shownMove the stack so the layer being shown is in the middleOther layers while one is shownThin frame around the layer being shownFrame and line colourName labels with a leader line+13 more

Hex tile cartogram (US states) · hexcartogram

Every US state as an equal hexagon with a 3D cube, glass sphere, circle or bar sized by its value — like the AAA gasoline-price map

  3. Drag the grid on the video to move it; change size, gap, labels, $ / % and colours in the settings.

◎Depth of field + continuous drift pan

Depth of field · dofblur

A camera focus band across the map — everything above and below goes soft, like a tilted lens; the focus can rack from near to far, labels can blur with it. Pair it with “Make the camera drift” for a continuous pan

Step by step

  1. Move the map to the place and tilt it, then click the button.
  2. The Depth of field + drift button also turns the scene into a continuous pan; on any depth-of-field layer press 🎥 Make the camera drift (distance, direction, tilt and turn are in the settings).
  3. Set where the focus starts and ends, the sharp band, the softness, blur strength and angle. Keep the layer at the top of the list so labels blur too.
  4. Open When it shows to set when it appears, how long it animates and when it hides (or Split at the playhead).

💡 Plays the sound from your reference clip — turn on Sound in Preview & export. The clip sounds are also in the sound library (Recorded clips).

Settings you can change

Drift distanceDrift directionCamera tilt for the driftSlow turn during the driftFocus starts atFocus ends atSharp band heightSoft transitionBlur strengthBand angleBlur labels and markers tooVignetteAmbienceSoundSound volume
Needs your own data or a live service — see the steps

Transit line · transit

  3. Press Finish (or double-click the last point).
